disposition_mapping.rationale: Extraction merges with comparative load because both share one tool class (read-only connector or validated manual upload) and one failure mode (data absent or ambiguous); separating them buys no diagnostic seam, only an extra handoff. The council corrected the initial 'pure retrieval' framing: locked-period cutoff is a cutoff discipline, not a data-quality guarantee, so the merged step carries a mandatory reconciliation gate with a named exception recipient, and the manual-upload path is specified as a permanent, first-class mode rather than a transitional fallback, since for a material share of entities it is the normal operating mode. VAR-R-01's required input (locked-period actuals) is preserved explicitly on the merged step.

Comparative load shares the retrieval tool class and failure mode with extraction, so it merges into the same step rather than being separately staged. Version ambiguity (which forecast cycle is 'latest', whether an approval tag is genuine) is treated as an explicit escalation condition, not silently inferred, preserving the judgment behind 'approved'/'latest' as a named, owned decision. VAR-R-02's required inputs (approved budget version, latest forecast) remain explicit inputs to the merged step.

The council rejected folding computation into the retrieval mega-step: computation reads a categorically different tool (a versioned methodology config) and fails by a categorically different mode (the formula doesn't apply to a structural break), which is a real architectural seam, not institutional habit. The step is restructured to make FX isolation and policy consistency explicit, inspectable outputs (satisfying KB-06/KB-07/KB-08) and to add a structural-item classification sub-function with confidence-based human routing, preventing silent misapplication of the standard decomposition to acquisitions, divestitures, or new SKUs. VAR-R-05 and VAR-R-06 required inputs are preserved explicitly.

Materiality screening remains its own step because its threshold config has a different owner and change-control cadence (CFO policy) than the methodology config in TS-02, and because the actor-separation control (VAR-R-04) depends on the reviewer being able to see what was mechanically selected versus what a human added or waived. It is restructured to add an append-only, attributed override layer distinct from the immutable mechanical-selection artifact, and to retain the full unselected variance population rather than discarding it. VAR-R-03's required input (materiality thresholds) is preserved, and VAR-R-08 (survival of the function) is satisfied by this distinct step.

Commentary gathering, unconstrained by design, is restructured to AI-drafted narrative with budget holders as confirming/editing exception reviewers rather than authors-from-blank-page. The council converged on hardening this against the single biggest accountability risk in the redesign: confirmation must be an explicit, identity-stamped, non-defaultable action (no timeout-as-approval), with escalation and an attributed FP&A-analyst fallback author, and the confirmation contract must be channel-agnostic so low-bandwidth or intermittently connected budget holders are not structurally excluded from real confirmation.

The council decisively rejected absorbing consolidation into the manager's review step: commentary-to-computed-driver consistency checking and completeness verification is preparer-level QC, different work by a different role for a different purpose than the manager's challenge, and folding it into review either eats review time or gets skipped under deadline pressure. It is restructured as a distinct step combining a deterministic consistency-check function with an irreducible human resolution role, producing a frozen, hash-logged artifact so the report reviewed and the report later regenerated are provably identical.

Review and challenge survives as a distinguishable, non-negotiable human judgment gate per VAR-R-07, carried by an actor (FP&A manager) distinct from the materiality config owner in TS-03, satisfying VAR-R-04. It is strengthened, not merely preserved as a checkpoint label: the reviewer's interface is contractually required to expose the mechanical-versus-override materiality layer, draft-versus-final commentary diffs, and structural-classification flags directly from the underlying artifacts, because a reviewer seeing only a polished narrative has nothing real to challenge. Rejection is modelled as a first-class, versioned loop back to upstream steps rather than an informal redo.

Distribution is restructured into gated, automatic publication of exactly the artifact approved at review, with full logging of what was sent, to whom, and when. The council rejected pure default push: the manager's approval event must carry an explicit publication-mode decision (auto-publish versus live walkthrough), and the live-walkthrough exception path is specified as a resourced, channel-appropriate capability (including low-bandwidth equivalents) rather than a capability that exists on paper and atrophies from disuse.

steps.description: On period lock, a retrieval function (automated connector or, as a permanent first-class alternative for entities without integrated feeds, a validated manual-upload path) pulls actuals from the closed period and loads the approved budget version and latest forecast as comparatives. Both outputs share one artifact contract: a versioned, checksummed dataset plus a reconciliation-status flag (tie-out pass/fail) and a version-resolution flag (which forecast cycle, confirmed-approved or not). Extraction and comparative load are merged because they share tool class (connector or validated upload) and failure mode (data absent or ambiguous); any reconciliation failure or version ambiguity halts the artifact and routes to a named FP&A analyst owner before it is marked ready for computation, rather than being resolved by guess or silently passed downstream. The manual-upload path is specified as a standing, budgeted mode of this step, not a transitional contingency, because for a material share of reporting entities it is the normal operating mode indefinitely.
steps.name: Triggered extraction and comparative load with reconciliation gate

steps.description: A computation function, distinct from retrieval because it reads a different tool (a versioned methodology config) and fails by a different mode (the formula does not apply, not that data is missing), computes price, volume and mix variances on actuals and budget prepared on the same accounting basis, applying accounting policies consistently (policy changes are logged as dated config diffs, never silent recalibration) and isolating FX at constant currency as an explicit, separately visible line, never blended into mix or other. A bounded classification heuristic flags items with no prior-period baseline or beyond a configured structural-break threshold (new SKU, discontinued line, M&A/divestiture volume); anything below a configured confidence score, and any item touching consolidation scope, routes to a named analyst for manual classification rather than being forced through the standard decomposition.
steps.name: Variance computation with structural-item classification

steps.description: A screening function, kept distinct from computation because it reads a separately owned, separately permissioned config (CFO/policy threshold table, a different change-control domain than the accounting methodology config in TS-02), applies the percentage and absolute materiality thresholds to produce an immutable mechanical-selection artifact. Analyst judgment additions (sub-threshold items flagged for strategic significance) or waivers (large but well-understood timing items) are recorded as a second, append-only, attributed event layer on top of that artifact, never as an in-place edit of the mechanical list, so the mechanical result and the discretionary result remain separately visible to every downstream consumer. The full, unselected variance population is retained, not discarded, so immateriality judgments remain reconstructible.
steps.name: Materiality screening with append-only override layer

steps.actor: Budget holders (with FP&A analyst as named fallback author)
steps.description: A drafting function generates a commentary draft for each selected variance from driver-level operational data and the TS-02/TS-03 outputs, with a confidence score. Confirmation is an explicit, identity-stamped action, enforced at the data-model level so no timeout, silence, or closed ticket can resolve to 'confirmed'; non-response is a distinct escalation event routed first to the budget holder's manager, then at a hard SLA cutoff to a named FP&A analyst whose fallback-authored commentary is tagged with their own attribution, never presented as the budget holder's. For wide-margin breaches or items unexplained for two consecutive periods, confirmation requires a substantive edit or annotation, not a bare accept. The confirmation contract is channel-agnostic: a full evidence panel for connected users, a lightweight structured form or email-reply equivalent for low-bandwidth or intermittently connected budget holders, with the same non-defaultable guarantee in both channels. Every draft-to-final diff is retained.
steps.name: AI-drafted commentary with gated, channel-agnostic confirmation
outputs: Budget holder commentary (confirmed, edited, or analyst-authored fallback, attributed)

steps.description: A checking function verifies, deterministically, that every selected variance has attached commentary, that each commentary's named driver matches the dominant driver in the TS-02 decomposition, and that the consolidated total reconciles to the P&L variance it purports to explain, producing a flagged-mismatch list. Resolving a flagged mismatch, and catching the class of error a driver-tag comparison cannot detect (a correctly labelled but implausible narrative), remains an irreducible analyst function. This step is retained as distinct from review because it is different work, by a different role, for a different purpose, than the manager's challenge in TS-06; folding it into review either slows the one calendar-anchored human gate the requirements protect or causes the check to be silently skipped under deadline pressure. Output is a frozen, hash-logged draft artifact: the exact bytes reviewed in TS-06 are the bytes reconstructible on demand.
inputs: Budget holder commentary (confirmed, edited, or analyst-authored fallback, attributed)
steps.name: Consistency-check and consolidation QC

steps.description: The FP&A manager, an actor distinct from the materiality config owner in TS-03, reviews and challenges the frozen draft report served from the underlying artifact store directly: the mechanical-versus-override materiality layer, the draft-versus-final commentary diffs, and the structural-classification flags are all visible, not flattened into a single polished narrative, so that challenge is exercised over judgment as well as arithmetic. Rejection is a first-class event that reopens a specific upstream artifact (TS-02 for recompute/reclassify, TS-04 for re-commentary) as a new, versioned cycle rather than an informal redo. The manager's approval event carries an explicit publication-mode decision (auto-publish versus route to live walkthrough), made deliberately at approval time.
steps.name: Review and challenge

steps.description: Publication fires only on the explicit decision captured at TS-06 approval, publishing exactly the frozen artifact version approved, with a log of precisely what was sent, to whom, and when, and the artifact hash attached so what management saw is permanently reconstructible. The default is automatic push to a governed, permissioned dashboard with role-based alerting on material items; where the approval decision routes to live walkthrough (board cycles, new-CFO scenarios, flagged material items, or low-bandwidth sites needing a dial-in/downloadable-deck equivalent), that capability is a resourced, named exception path, not an unused capability that exists only on paper.
steps.name: Governed publication and distribution
